title: Dispatch: atomic clock/stable-recovery + rest evidence (attempt 1)
description:
Works defect beads eshyra-r2ps AND eshyra-cc3c together (read both first: full analysis with file/line refs). Parent spec: eshyra-geny (acceptance criteria 3 and 4).

Branch/worktree: this bead's id, cut from eshyra-geny.

## Code survey (verified 2026-07-19)

- `packages/core/src/state/rest.ts:159-219` `advanceWorldTime`: clock update, effect expiry, and short-rest-window closure commit inside one `withTransaction`; `resolveStableRecoveries` then runs at line 217 AFTER the transaction returned, against the raw connection.
- `packages/core/src/state/hpLifecycle.ts:597-626` `resolveStableRecoveries`: maps due rows through `adjustHp(db, 1, ...)`, each opening its own transaction.
- `packages/core/src/state/rest.ts:588-611` `complete()`: passes its own `txn` to `advanceWorldTime` (so that path nests), then builds `benefits` copying `expiredEffects`, `previousElapsedMinutes`, `elapsedMinutes`, `inGameTime`, `narrativeLabelStale`, `closedRecoveryWindows` from the time result — but omits `stableRecoveries`. `benefits` is both the tool response and persisted `benefits_json` (line 684-688).
- `withTransaction` (`persistence/db.ts:12`) uses better-sqlite3 `db.transaction`, which nests as savepoints — so moving the recovery calls inside the callback composes correctly.
- Check all consumers of `advanceWorldTime`'s result (`WorldClock` shape) and of `resolveStableRecoveries` before changing shapes: orchestrator/toolRest.ts, rest.ts, tests, internal.ts exports.

## Required behavior changes

1. eshyra-r2ps: resolve all due stable recoveries INSIDE the same `withTransaction` callback as the clock transition in `advanceWorldTime`, returning them as part of that atomic result (no post-transaction mutation). The `WorldClock` result shape keeps its `stableRecoveries` field.
2. eshyra-cc3c: add `stableRecoveries: time.stableRecoveries` to the `benefits` object in `complete()` so it reaches both the tool response and persisted `benefits_json`.

## Tests

- Atomicity (rest.test.ts or hpLifecycle.test.ts, follow existing setup helpers): with a due stable recovery arranged, inject a failure during recovery resolution (e.g. corrupt the second due character's row so `adjustHp` throws, or another deterministic injection) and assert the clock's `elapsed_minutes` did NOT advance and no partial recovery persisted.
- Evidence: a short rest whose window crosses a stable character's recovery deadline → returned benefits contain the recovery (character id, HP transition), and the persisted `rest_event.benefits_json` contains the same; the character wakes at 1 HP.

## Verification

`npm run verify:worktree` from this worktree (run `npm ci` first). Do not weaken existing tests. Commit on this branch only.
